about: Running record of what we have done on the desk: every change, test and decision, newest first. Entries are only ever added, never edited or removed. Add one entry per working session (see CLAUDE.md).

entries.title: 10:52 desk update: news refresh and unlock re-check (v5 rules)
did: Refreshed the public news: bitcoin just under $60,000 as Asian chip stocks slide, today's PCE report, tariffs still pending. 158 claims checked over 3 rounds, 25 removed or corrected (three briefs dropped because their pages could not be opened).
Re-researched and independently re-checked 32 shortable unlocks in the next 30 days; skipped 4 marked can't-short in shortable.json (WPAY, ADI, RAIN, YZY).
Added COAI (25 Nov, 19.54M) after a KuCoin USDT perp listing was confirmed. Did not add ASTER, TRUMP, WLD or MORPHO: their 'dates' are slices of continuous streams, not real unlock events.
found: Trackers disagree on IRYS (tokenomics.com ~1.18B lump today vs Tokenomist: none until 25 Dec), GRVT (29 vs 30 Nov), GUN (28 vs 30 Nov), M (2 vs 12 Dec) and WET (192.5M vs 256.67M): all marked disputed.
Impact grade changes: H Very high->High, SUI ->Low, TON Moderate->High, MOVE High->Moderate, SEI ->Moderate, MON ->Very high.
decided: Left ether's snapshot price blank: no timestamped figure could be confirmed this run (live prices still load in the browser).

entries.title: v5: only unlocks we can short; never MEXC
did: Coach K's new rule: check every token has a perp/futures market we can short, focus only on those, and avoid MEXC because of sanctions.

Checked the MEXC claim: FinCEN (US Treasury) issued an order on 6 Nov 2026 cutting MEXC off from the US financial system over at least $16B of transactions tied to sanctions evasion and cybercrime (fincen.gov/system/files/2026-11/MEXC-Section-9714.pdf). Strictly it's a FinCEN order, not OFAC sanctions, but US firms that deal with MEXC face enforcement risk.
Rules frozen as v5 (data/strategy_v5.json): v4 minus MEXC, plus the focus rule.

New scripts/shortable.py checks every unlock on the list twice a day on GitHub and writes data/shortable.json (yes / no / unknown, with where it trades and when it was checked). The brief, the Picks tab and the Unlocks tab now list only shortable unlocks; can't-short ones sit behind a click.
The 4-hourly research task now skips deep research for unlocks marked can't short.
found: KNTQ (27 Dec) was only on MEXC, so under v5 it can't be shorted.
decided: 'Can't short' is a fact only when every allowed exchange answered (Binance, Bybit via CoinGecko, OKX, Bitget, Gate, Hyperliquid, KuCoin). If any couldn't be reached it's 'unknown' and stays on the list until rechecked.

entries.title: v4: short on other exchanges when Binance has no perp
did: Coach K asked to check where every token trades and short it on another exchange instead of skipping; and to skip only after confirming as fact that it can't be shorted.

Tested which free exchange APIs GitHub's servers can reach: OKX, Bitget, Gate, Hyperliquid, KuCoin, MEXC and CoinGecko yes; Bybit and Binance's live API no (data/venue_probe.json). Bybit's perp list comes via CoinGecko.
New scripts/venues.py: lists each exchange's USDT perps, gets UTC daily candles (and open interest on OKX/Gate), and confirms by price that a ticker is the same token.
Rules frozen as v4 (data/strategy_v4.json): v3 unchanged, plus other exchanges. Brief cards now show where each token has perps and which exchange to short on.
found: Ticker matches lie: 'ADI' on OKX, Bitget, Gate and Bybit is a ~$300+ stock perp (most likely Analog Devices; OKX files it under stocks), while ADI Chain is ~$7. Three exchanges agreeing with each other did not prove anything, so CoinGecko's price is the main check and stock tickers can't be confirmed by agreement.
The unlock records' implied price can be weeks old (JCT: $0.011 implied vs $0.0016 now on Binance and OKX).

Survey of current candidates (data/venue_survey.json): ADI 9 Dec can't be shorted anywhere (confirmed on all 8 exchanges); KNTQ 27 Dec is only on MEXC (price confirmed) but MEXC has no open-interest history, so as a first insider unlock it will be skipped; every other candidate trades on Binance plus 4-6 other exchanges.
Off-Binance evidence is thin: 4 historic trades on Bybit/Gate-only tokens (+5.5R total).
decided: A 'can't short it' skip is made only when all 8 exchanges answered and none lists the real token; if any can't be reached, it stays on watch and is rechecked.
Off Binance, short on the confirmed exchange with the most dollar volume over 7 days. Bybit-only tokens get no call (no Bybit candles from the server).

found: CoinMarketCap and Binance agreed on BTC near $59,500-59,650 but disagreed on 24h changes and on ether/solana, so only the BTC price was kept; CoinGecko's page returned a stale-looking $27,408 and was ignored.
Unconfirmed release times (jobless claims, new home sales, the 08:00 UTC options expiry time) and the '14 other economies' tariff count were removed; Tuesday's ETF flows were not yet published.

entries.title: Morning brief page on the website
did: Put the morning brief on the GitHub site as its own page (brief.html), linked from the Picks tab: short today, open shorts, coming up, the record, and every call so far with its result.

A free GitHub job rebuilds it every morning at 23:41 UTC (06:41 Bangkok) and keeps one snapshot per morning in data/briefs/ (pick any past morning from the dropdown). The twice-daily trade-log job also refreshes it with the logged calls.
decided: The website page is the permanent record; the Claude artifact version is optional.

entries.title: Morning brief dashboard
did: Built 'Unlock shorts: morning brief' (https://claude.ai/artifact/Mh3h6x2jFDn2q2eeetmrxn): one simple page with what to short today, open shorts with levels, coming-up setups and what each still needs, the record, and the last 30 days of closed trades.
Added scripts/morning_brief.py (read-only, frozen v3 rules) and a scheduled task, 'Crypto Desk: morning unlock-short brief', that rebuilds it every day at 06:41 Bangkok, before the 07:00 entry.
found: 25 Nov: nothing to short today; MON and GRVT open (late calls, not counted); WET (entry 2 Dec) and CYS (4 Dec, needs open interest down 10%+) coming up.
decided: The dashboard website stays as the full desk; the brief is the simple daily execution view.

entries.title: Daily unlock re-check (10:52 Bangkok run)
did: Re-researched 37 unlock rows (next 7 days, stale checks, and every row under 60 confidence), then had separate agents re-check 38 rows: 2 confirmed, 35 partial, 1 contradicted (M, 2 Dec vs Tokenomist's 12 Dec).
Added GUN (30 Nov) and STO (3 Dec); left out PMT and ON (single tracker only) and STABLE 8 Dec (tracker is out of date: the lock moved to Dec 2027).
Refreshed news.json: 3 stories, 6 briefs, 12 calendar rows; 79 claims checked over 2 rounds, 9 removed.

LIT's next unlock moved from 30 to 27 Dec and is now shown as a monthly amount (~13.9M LIT).
Web search ran out partway through the re-check, so most re-checks re-opened cited sources rather than finding new ones.
decided: Keep phantom-risk rows out: an unlock needs at least one opened source showing a real transfer on that date.

entries.title: History tab and this journal
did: ARIA (unlock 21 Nov) disappeared from Trade signals once its date passed. Added the History tab: a permanent, searchable log of every unlock the desk has shown (data/archive.json, scripts/archive.py), rebuilt from the repo history: 104 unlocks.
Started this journal so every change and decision stays findable.
found: ARIA was graded AA but flagged pumped (+210% in 30 days) and was never a v3 pick (8.3% of circulating, not a first insider unlock). The standard short was stopped on entry day; ARIA was +38% from the day −7 open by the day after the unlock.
decided: Nothing is deleted from History or this journal; both update twice a day or whenever we work.

entries.title: Entry days, exit days and taking profit early
did: Tested shorting 14, 7 and 3 days before the unlock against covering 1, 3, 7 and 14 days after, an entry zone (thirds at −14/−7/−3), and closing 60% at the 35% target with a trailing stop on the rest.
Added 'Compare entries and exits' to every pick: profit from each entry day to each exit day, a live 'now' price, and a shadow result for the 60% + trailing exit.
found: Fair test (each trade picked only with what was known on its entry day): day −7 +0.74R a trade, day −14 +0.28R, day −3 +0.42R. A first run that made day −14 look best was using day −7 information.
Entry zone: more winners (64%) but less profit (+0.64R).
60% at target + 40% trailing 10%: +0.86R vs +0.81R for the current exit — inside the noise.
decided: Keep day −7 entry and the current exit. Track the 60%/trailing exit as a shadow result; adopt only if live trades back it (would be v4).

entries.title: Bybit and Gate.io perpetuals
did: Mapped which tokens had a Bybit or Gate.io perpetual before Binance (75) and researched 55 new ones; independent re-check of every qualifying unlock; priced them from Bybit/Gate through Coach K's browser.
found: 4 more v3 trades with unchanged rules: 3 won, +5.5R (DBR, FLOW, BOBA won; TAIKO stopped then fell 43%).
The open-interest rule skipped three first-insider unlocks that all won (RAY, ATH, HAEDAL) — a watch item.
decided: Keep the frozen rules. Live picks stay Binance-only because Bybit/Gate block the cloud servers; proposed running a small script on the Mac mini (no answer yet).

entries.title: 2021–2025 history test
did: Researched 122 tokens with Binance perpetuals back to 2021; re-checked every tradeable unlock before pricing.
found: Big one-day unlocks are mostly a 2023+ thing; many 2021–22 big unlocks had no perpetual to short; about a third of 'unlocks' were swaps, re-locks, delays or launches.
v3 took 5 trades: 3 won, +5.5R. Both losses came with BTC up 28–47% the month before.
decided: No rule change; BTC trend is a watch item.

entries.title: Picks tab and live test start (v3 rules frozen)
did: Froze the v3 rules in data/strategy_v3.json. Picks tab: only v3 setups, called once on entry day and logged in data/picks_log.json, never rewritten.
First live call: HUMA (taken 19 Nov), stopped on entry day (−1R). The desk's data later cut HUMA's size from 26% to 13%, so on today's data it would not qualify; the call stays as made.
decided: Pass mark: after 30 live trades, average above +0.25R. Any rule change becomes v4 with a new date.

entries.title: Chart study: open interest is the tell (v3)
did: Tested chart, volume, funding and open-interest signals on 917 unlocks using Binance's free files.
found: Open interest falling 10%+ the week before entry turns first insider unlocks under 25% from break-even (+0.07R) into winners (+0.78R, 69% won); confirmed on 818 routine unlocks it wasn't found on.
v3 backtest: 56 trades, 62% won, +0.75R a trade, worst drawdown −3.9% at 1% risk.
decided: v3: take 25%+ unlocks, and first insider unlocks only if open interest fell 10%+; skip anything pumped 30%+.

entries.title: Take / skip groups and the backtest journal sheet
did: Sorted every past unlock into take full size, take half size and skip; built the shareable journal sheet.
found: Only 25%+ unlocks that weren't pumped made money in both data sets on their own; routine unlocks lost (−50.7R over 820).
decided: Dropped 'already falling the week before' as a rule (did not hold on unseen data).

entries.title: First unseen-data test (2023–25)
did: Froze the 18 Nov rules, researched 62 big Binance tokens, re-checked every unlock independently, priced them.
found: The strict rule was NOT PROVEN after the re-check: 13 trades, +0.53R a trade, bad-case range below zero.
decided: Keep testing; don't sell the strategy to followers until proven.

entries.title: Pump study and best/worst trades
did: Studied what pumps into and after unlocks do, the best and worst trades and why; tested trailing stops.
found: Tokens pumped 30%+ going in lose; most losers were right on direction but squeezed through the stop first; trailing stops didn't help.
decided: Skip anything pumped 30%+ into the unlock.

entries.title: Rules into the tracker, more past tokens, simpler dashboard
did: Added the new rules and pump warnings to the tracker and signals; looped in 69 past tokens; size badges for big unlocks; moved the busy panels behind clicks.
decided: Keep the dashboard simple with extras behind a click.
